subject: Urgent: P99 tail latency spike — mitigation plan + customer comms
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, ethan.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: high p99 tail on hosted-rw-prod - first alert

Team —

Monitoring triggered at 09:07 PST: a sustained p99 latency increase (token generation path) on hosted-rw-prod starting ~08:55 and peaking at ~09:04. Impact is concentrated on longer-context sessions (>2k tokens), throughput drop ~25% on those shards; overall 95th looks OK. We've collected live KV cache hit rates and a diagnostic snapshot (attached).

Immediate steps I've kicked off:
- Circuit opened to route new requests to the canary lower-memory quantized variant for one region (us-west-2) — temp fallback.
- Increased worker concurrency for non-burst queues by +15% to maintain throughput.
- Collected profiles and KV cache metrics (see incident-stats-20260228.csv).

Ask from SRE: can product/CS prepare a short external status note for any customers we proactively contact? Prefer a factual note: what happened, affected scope, mitigation in place, ETA for fix.

I'll keep digging, sending updates every 30-45m.

Dylan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-stats-20260228.csv, diag-snapshot-20260228.tar.gz

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, ethan.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: high p99 tail on hosted-rw-prod - first alert

Quick technical update:

- Root cause (prelim): we see increased KV cache eviction churn on the long-context workload after a recent kernel selector tweak pushed by the runtime team in the last deploy (2026-02-26). That tweak favors memory-local kernels but under certain sequence-length mixes it increases cache pressure.
- Short-term mitigation (we can apply in 20m): rollback the kernel selector change for the impacted model family in us-west-2 and expand the canary fallback to us-east-1. This should reduce p99 to baseline within ~30–60 minutes post-rollback.
- Mid-term: we need an opt-in policy that pins kernel selector per-model-profile and a QA pass with 95/99 tail coverage on the next release. ETA for mid-term patch: 1 sprint (2 weeks).

I will coordinate the rollback with SRE (Dylan) now. If Product needs a customer-friendly explanation say: "an infrastructure-level kernel selection change caused unexpected memory pressure for long-context sessions; we've reverted the change for affected models and are working on a durable selector policy." Avoid suggesting data loss or model degradation.

Marcus
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

Subject: Re: high p99 tail on hosted-rw-prod - first alert

Megan — apologies for the delay in formal customer outreach. Quick status update and next steps: 

- What happened: a runtime kernel selection change increased KV cache eviction for long-context sessions, which produced transient p99 latency spikes on certain shards.
- Scope: affected sessions were primarily long-context chat sessions in US regions (us-west-2 and us-east-1). We did NOT see embeddings-only endpoints affected.
- Mitigation completed: 2026-02-28 11:00 PST — SRE rolled back the kernel selector change in the impacted pools and extended the canary fallback. Post-rollback telemetry shows p99 within acceptable SLOs; monitoring remained green after rollback.
- ETA / next steps: Marcus will schedule a runtime patch that pins selector behavior per-model profile (planned release in one sprint). We will provide a postmortem with timeline and remediation steps by 2026-03-05 COB.

For Greenfield specifically: we confirmed no lost requests and no model regressions. If you prefer, we can schedule a 15-minute sync before your demos to confirm everything looks green on your end.

Attached is a short customer-facing note (draft_customer_notice_v1.md) — feel free to edit; we'll send from my account once approved.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_customer_notice_v1.md
